explanation: It grew from the Arabic spoken in medieval Sicily and Malta, then took many words from Italian, Sicilian and English. Everyday words such as numbers stay close to Arabic.

claims.text: Maltese, written in the Latin alphabet, is a Semitic language descended from the Arabic spoken in medieval Sicily and Malta.
Maltese is not a Romance, Germanic or Celtic language, though it has many Italian and English loanwords.
Maltese has taken many words from Italian, Sicilian and English.
Maltese numbers such as wieħed, tnejn and tlieta (one, two, three) are close to their Arabic equivalents.
